name: Squire Village (Squire Village Apartments)
headline: Related Affordable, with Maiker Housing Partners as special limited partner, is buying and renovating Squire Village, a 1982 complex of about 50 one-bedroom project-based Section 8 apartments for seniors on Grant Drive in Northglenn. It won a 2025 federal 4% credit award from CHFA, and Maiker sold $13.3M of Fannie Mae MBS-backed bonds for it in July 2026.
why_it_matters: A small Section 8 senior preservation deal: the buyer extends the Section 8 use agreement by 20 years and the tax credit restrictions from 2033 to 2056, and $3.7M ($75,000 a unit) of rehab is funded mostly by bonds, a taxable mortgage and 4% equity.

status.label: Bonds priced July 2026; acquisition closing and rehab start not confirmed
status.detail: Maiker's $13,295,000 bonds sold on 2026-07-23 with a dated date of 2026-07-30, which suggests the acquisition financing closed around then (inferred). No public record confirms the recorded sale or the start of renovation; the 2025 plan had renovation running from February 2026 to January 2027.

next_step: Watch for the recorded deed to Squire Village Preservation, L.P., Northglenn building permits for the rehab, and the new LURA.

key_numbers.meaning: CHFA's award lists 16 at 30% AMI and 34 at 60% AMI; city and owner documents describe 51 senior units with project-based Section 8.
About $11.4M over 10 years; no state credit. The 2025 plan expected $7,858,000 of equity.
Fannie Mae MBS-secured; CHFA's award shows $10,019,950 of bond cap.
From the buyer's 2025 budget; rehab about $3.7M, or $75,000 a unit.

background.text: The buyer told Northglenn in 2025 that it was under contract to buy the property with all control rights and would form a new single-purpose entity before closing. The seller is not named in public records found.

A 2022 zoning report in the city packet was prepared for Wells Fargo Multifamily Capital for a Fannie Mae loan and lists Related Fund Management entities as reliance parties, which suggests a Related affiliate was already involved with the property's financing in 2022 (inferred).

Northglenn City Council passed CR-77 7-0 on 2025-08-11, assigning the city's $2,460,746 2025 bond cap to CHFA for Squire Village, with CHFA to use it elsewhere in the city if the project did not proceed.
Maiker held a TEFRA hearing on 2026-04-16 with no objections, and the Adams County commissioners approved up to $18M of bonds 5-0; the clerk certified the resolution on 2026-05-05.
The 2025 timeline targeted a tax credit closing on 2026-01-01, renovation from 2026-02-01 to 2027-01-01, stabilization by 2027-04-01 and Forms 8609 by 2027-07-01.
Maiker sold bonds for another Related Affordable deal, Dawson Square Apartments ($12,970,000), in the same week.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award lists the deal as family housing, while the city packet and CHFA's own LIHTC property list describe it as elderly housing.
CHFA's award and LIHTC list show 50 units, while the city packet and the Adams County resolution describe about 51 units.
CHFA's award puts 16 units at 30% AMI and 34 at 60% AMI, while the buyer's 2025 memo says all units will be at or below 60% AMI.
CHFA prints the address as 11180 Grant Drive, while the county resolution and the city memo use 11170 Grant Drive.
CHFA shows $10,019,950 of bonds and the 2025 plan expected about $6.4M, while Maiker sold $13,295,000 of bonds in July 2026.

open_questions: Seller, recorded sale price and deed date (the Adams County assessor site could not be reached; the 2025 budget shows $14.5M for acquisition).
How the city's 2025 cap assigned to CHFA relates to the Maiker-issued bonds, and the final split of bond cap sources.
Section 8 HAP contract terms and expiration after the deal.
General contractor, rehab start date and whether residents stay in place during renovation.
